_tuning_notes: Taiga grizzly, the diet-system showcase. diet.hunts = entity ids fished/hunted when hungry (paw-swipe at salmon in water within 12, 40% per swipe, hardcoded); diet.scavenges reserved for shared use with the vulture. special.berry_raiding also needs mobGriefing. Mother-aggro: hurting a cub or standing within 6 blocks of one angers every adult within 16. Sleeps at night in shelter — day is the threat window. Phase 3: salmon (diet) baits cage traps; needs the reinforced tier. RARITY: tier 'uncommon' supplies the spawn weight; group_size and nearby_cap are pinned here (1-3, cap 3). nearby_cap denies natural spawns when that many of this animal are already within 64 blocks — the fix for persistent CREATURE mobs accumulating forever. BABY SIZE 0.4.2: baby_scale moved 0.5 -> 1.0. The client already bakes the baby mesh through vanilla's BabyModelTransform (body halved, head full size) and vanilla age scaling halves the hitbox, so a 0.5 here was a SECOND shrink and calves rendered at a quarter of adult size. 1.0 = vanilla baby proportions. SIZE PASS 0.4.6: scale set against MEASURED vanilla hitboxes rather than by eye (cow 0.90x1.40, horse 1.40x1.60, polar bear 1.40x1.40, ravager 1.95x2.20, wolf 0.60x0.85, turtle 1.20x0.40, ocelot 0.60x0.70, chicken 0.40x0.70). Attributes.SCALE is uniform and multiplies the MODEL and the HITBOX together, so this is the one lever that cannot desync them. 1.07x polar bear width, 1.15x its height — at or above the vanilla bear, as intended. SIZE PASS revised: the first attempt scaled an already-wrong box. Measuring the baked meshes showed the hitboxes never matched the models — the hippo mesh was 1.06 blocks tall inside a 1.60 box (66% fill, a third of it empty air), while the gorilla mesh was LARGER than its hitbox (121%). Builder dimensions in MenagerieEntities now match the measured mesh, and this scale multiplies model and hitbox together from there, so the drawn animal fills the box it is struck in.
guide_blurb: Fish thief, berry burglar, terrible alarm clock.
